schemaNote: v0.2 is a strict superset of v0.1 adding protocolVersion, multipleTestingCorrection, environment, humanAuthorization, and controls. v0.1 could not express four of RESEARCH-METHOD.md's twelve required fields; see run constraint SCH-001. Other experiments remain on v0.1 pending a separate migration PR.
question: Can the evaluator prevent recorded copies from adding evidence and incomplete coverage from proving absence?
null: At least one recorded copy changes evidential mass or one incomplete search yields absence.
target: Zero violations in exhaustive small worlds and one million frozen randomized worlds.

population.description: Synthetic knowledge-transaction worlds. A world is one claim type, one search ledger of location statuses, and one evidence ledger of (rootId, side) records. No natural-language content, no real entities, no personal data.

exhaustive.method: complete cartesian enumeration within declared bounds
exhaustive.worldCountDerivation: sum(4^L for L in 1..4) = 340 location ledgers; sum(6^R for R in 0..3) = 259 evidence ledgers; 340 * 259 * 2 claim types = 176120

searchSpace.definition: For this conformance kernel the searched space is the space of worlds, not a space of real locations. The exhaustive phase enumerates it completely within the declared bounds above; absence of a violation is therefore admissible only for worlds inside those bounds.
searchSpace.enumerationMethod: deterministic nested iteration in src/kl000_worlds.py, verified against declaredWorldCount before any invariant is evaluated
searchSpace.boundedAbsenceStatement: Zero violations across the exhaustive phase supports 'no violation exists within the declared bounds' and supports nothing about worlds outside them. This is the same discipline KL-000 tests in the evaluator, applied to KL-000's own result.

rootDefinition.root: An evidence root is the value of a record's rootId field. Root identity is declared operationally by the transaction author; it is not inferred, proved semantically, or verified against any external issuer.
rootDefinition.copy: Two records are copies of one another when they carry the same rootId. A copy may differ in every other respect, including record id.
rootDefinition.sharedDependency: Not representable in schema v0.1. Partial dependence between two distinct rootIds cannot be expressed, so this experiment cannot test it. Recorded as a limit, not tested as a hypothesis.
rootDefinition.independence: Distinct rootId values are treated as independent by assumption. KL-000 tests that the evaluator honours declared independence, not that the declaration is true.

baselines.description: Concludes from record count alone, ignoring roots entirely.
baselines.expectedOutcome: MUST FAIL copy invariance (I1). Its failure is the positive control proving the checker has power to detect a violation.

baselines.description: Counts distinct roots but ignores the search ledger.
Full root collapse, no coverage requirement for absence.
Full coverage accounting, counts records rather than roots.

controlsNote: C09 and C10 are preregistered as INDISTINGUISHABLE to this evaluator. Schema v0.1 has no field linking an evidence record to a search location, so the evaluator cannot know where a counterexample was found. For absence claims this is conservative and safe -- any counterexample refutes absence regardless of provenance -- so identical treatment is preregistered as the EXPECTED and PERMITTED outcome, not as a violation. The unverifiable case, a receipt asserting a location was unavailable while also carrying evidence from it, is preregistered as a known blind spot and reported as such whatever the result.
primaryEndpoint: count of hard-invariant violations, target exactly 0
secondaryEndpoints: count of fail-closed rejections, by cause
baseline violation counts, which must be non-zero for B1-B4
wall-clock and worlds-per-second, for reproduction budgeting

invariants.name: copy invariance
invariants.statement: Appending a duplicate of any existing record (same rootId, same side) leaves conclusion, distinctRoots, supportingRoots, opposingRoots, margin, and conversionsToReverse unchanged, and increases records and repeatedRecordsCollapsed by exactly 1 each.

invariants.name: bounded absence
invariants.statement: conclusion == 'absent_within_declared_scope' implies search.complete is true and opposingRoots is empty. Equivalently no absence conclusion is reachable while any location status is not 'searched'.

invariants.name: side separation
invariants.statement: If any rootId appears with both sides, evaluation raises and no receipt is produced.

invariants.name: deterministic replay
invariants.statement: Evaluating the same world twice yields byte-identical canonical JSON and an equal contentDigest.

invariants.name: counterexample dominance
invariants.statement: For absence claims, a non-empty opposingRoots implies conclusion == 'present', at any coverage level.

invariants.name: digest integrity
invariants.statement: verify_content_digest holds for every emitted receipt, and fails for every single-field mutation of one.

invariants.name: order invariance
invariants.statement: Permuting locations or records changes no evidential field, no conclusion, and no contentDigest.

invariants.name: search arithmetic
invariants.statement: declared == len(locations), searched and unavailable equal their status counts, searched + unavailable <= declared, and complete == (searched == declared).

invariants.name: fail-closed parsing
invariants.statement: Malformed input raises an exception and never returns a receipt.

invariants.name: copies never mint roots
invariants.statement: distinctRoots equals the number of distinct rootId values in the input, and appending any number of copies of existing roots leaves it unchanged.

effectSize.statement: This is a conformance kernel, not a comparative one. The endpoint is a count with a target of exactly zero, so there is no minimum detectable effect to declare: a single violation rejects the invariant.
effectSize.powerOfTest: Test power is established by the baselines rather than by a sample-size calculation. B1-B4 are ablated evaluators that MUST be caught. If any of them passes, the checker is vacuous and the run is invalidated regardless of what B5 does.

uncertainty.exhaustivePhase: No sampling uncertainty. Zero violations across a complete enumeration is exact within the declared bounds and says nothing outside them.
uncertainty.randomizedPhase: Zero violations in n = 1,000,000 draws gives a 95% upper bound on per-world violation probability of 3/n = 3.0e-6 by the rule of three. This bounds a rate; it does not establish zero.
uncertainty.familyWise: Ten invariants are checked. Under a Bonferroni-style adjustment to 99.5% per invariant, the per-invariant upper bound becomes approximately 5.3/n = 5.3e-6. Both bounds are reported.
uncertainty.whatItCannotShow: Neither phase can show the invariants hold for worlds outside the declared bounds, for shared dependencies the schema cannot express, or for any real-world evidence process.

multipleTestingCorrection.method: none applied to the primary endpoint
multipleTestingCorrection.justification: No null-hypothesis significance test is performed. The primary endpoint is a violation count with target zero, and any violation rejects regardless of which invariant produced it. Bonferroni is reported only for the secondary rule-of-three rate bound, where ten simultaneous bounds are stated.

successCondition: Zero hard-invariant violations across the exhaustive phase, the randomized phase, and the adversarial suite, AND non-zero violation counts for each of B1-B4 confirming the checker has power.
failureCondition: One or more hard-invariant violations by B5. This rejects the invariant, sets KL-000 to failed, and blocks promotion of every downstream kernel.
invalidationCondition: Any of: the generator emits a world outside declared bounds; the enumerated world count differs from declaredWorldCount; the evaluator source hash differs from evaluatorUnderTest below; the frozen seed does not reproduce an identical world stream; any baseline B1-B4 records zero violations. An invalidated run is marked incomplete, never negative and never positive.
stopCondition: One violation rejects the invariant and blocks every downstream kernel. The confirmatory run halts on the first hard violation and preserves it with its full world.

frozenSeedsOrSplits.rng: Python stdlib random.Random, seeded per phase, no OS entropy
frozenSeedsOrSplits.splitPolicy: No train/test split applies. The exhaustive phase is not sampled and the randomized phase is generated once and consumed once.

protocolCommitNote: Assigned by git to the commit introducing this file. Recorded post-commit in PROTOCOL-COMMIT.txt and STATUS.json rather than by editing this file, so that the preregistration is never modified after it is frozen. The scientifically load-bearing freeze is evaluatorUnderTest, the declared bounds, and the seed, all of which are inside this file.

evaluatorUnderTest.note: KL-000 tests this evaluator as-is. No evaluator behaviour is changed by this experiment. If a violation is found, it is reported, not fixed within the confirmatory run.

environment.reproductionInterpreter: any CPython 3.11+; the experiment uses only json, hashlib, random, itertools, argparse from the standard library
environment.determinismNote: Results must be byte-identical across interpreters and platforms. Any platform-dependent output invalidates the run rather than being explained away.

safetyBoundary.dataClass: synthetic only; no personal, patient, sealed, classified, or legally restricted data
safetyBoundary.decisionAuthority: none; this experiment controls no medical, legal, governmental, financial, or physical action
safetyBoundary.network: no network access required or used
safetyBoundary.spend: zero; no metered service is invoked

humanAuthorization.requiredForExecutionReason: Offline, synthetic, zero-spend, no live decision authority, no restricted data.

requiredFor.action: publishing this branch or its base to the public github remote
requiredFor.status: not granted at preregistration time; referred to the founder

requiredFor.action: promoting any KL-000 result into CANONICAL-RECORDS.md or PUBLIC-CLAIMS.md
requiredFor.status: not sought by this run; promotion is a separate commit after founder review
out of scope; KL-011 has not passed

claimDiscipline.strongestSupportedIfPassed: Within the declared bounds, the reference evaluator did not allow a recorded copy to change evidential mass, and did not allow an incomplete search to yield an absence conclusion.
claimDiscipline.nearestUnsupportedExtension: That the dual ledger recovers truth, that declared roots are genuinely independent, that the invariants hold outside the declared bounds, or that any real-world evidence process is improved. None of these follow from a conformance result.
claimDiscipline.ifFailed: Recorded as a rejection of the invariant with the full counterexample world preserved. The counterexample is added to the permanent suite and downstream promotion is blocked.
